author: Knewz Staff
title: Records show Ken Paxton's campaign took $40,000 from donors linked to Chinese real estate investments in Texas - NewsBreak
text:
By Knewz Staff ,
21 hours ago Ken Paxton discusses foreign investment and Texas land ownership. BY: MEGA. Republican candidate Ken Paxton ’s campaign is facing renewed scrutiny after campaign finance records showed it received about $40,000 from donors connected to Texas real estate development involving Chinese investors.
The contributions came before the June 30 filing deadline, while Paxton and allied groups were spending millions on advertisements accusing Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico of supporting Chinese interests.
Most of the money reportedly came from executives associated with Wan Bridge, a US-based real estate company that solicits foreign investment for Texas housing projects.
The issue has emerged as Chinese investment, foreign land ownership, and national security become prominent subjects in the Texas Senate race.
The donations behind the scrutiny Paxton has made Chinese influence a key issue in his Senate campaign. BY: MEGA. Wan Bridge cofounder Ting Qiao gave nearly $30,000 to Paxton and political action committees connected to him between June 2025 and April 2026, Houston Chronicle reported.
Danting Li, another Wan Bridge cofounder and chief operating officer, gave slightly more than $10,000 through two donations in 2025.
Both executives are based in Texas, according to their social media profiles.
John Chiang, a third donor, works as an executive at Houston development firm Sueba.
The company works with Wan Bridge and America Modern Green, a US subsidiary of Chinese developer Modern Land.
Qiao previously worked at Modern Land for more than a decade and became an executive vice president.
Li worked for two years at America Modern Green in investor relations. Modern Land has a Communist Party branch, according to the outlet.
Wan Bridge operates housing developments in Houston, Dallas, and Austin.
Its Chinese-language website also promotes investment opportunities and describes operations connecting investors in China with US projects.
Paxton’s focus on China Paxton’s campaign finance records show donations linked to Texas real estate investors. BY: MEGA. The donations surfaced while Paxton and his allies were spending millions on advertisements attacking Talarico over China-related legislation.
The report noted that Paxton’s PAC, Lone Star Liberty, spent more than $7 million on an ad accusing Talarico of helping communist China.
Another ad costing more than $3 million warned that China was buying Texas property.
Paxton has pointed to his record as attorney general, including investigations and lawsuits involving companies with alleged Chinese government ties.
KABB reported that Paxton discussed the issue Tuesday at a VFW post near Joint Base San Antonio-Randolph.
He cited a Chinese billionaire’s purchase of more than 100,000 acres near Laughlin Air Force Base as a national security concern.
Paxton also criticized Talarico over votes against Senate Bill 17 and Senate Bill 667.
SB 17 restricts certain foreign ownership of Texas land, while SB 667 addresses state investments involving companies controlled by the Chinese government.
Talarico pushes back James Talarico faces attacks over his record on Chinese investment legislation. BY: MEGA. Talarico’s spokesperson rejected Paxton’s criticism, saying, “Ken Paxton is lying about James again because he can’t defend his career of corruption. Paxton is the only candidate in this race that has cozied up to the Chinese Communist Party, going on a lavish all expenses paid trip to China and meeting with CCP officials while he was supposed to be serving us.”
They further added, “There’s a reason Republicans call him ‘Commie Ken.’ James has voted to support Texans’ security, privacy, and first amendment protections from foreign government influence.”
Meanwhile, Chinese buyers accounted for 11% of foreign US real estate purchases in 2026, according to the National Association of Realtors.
Canada and Mexico remained the largest sources of foreign buyers, while Texas ranked third among destinations after California and Florida.

Wan Bridge cofounder Ting Qiao gave nearly $30,000 to Paxton and political action committees connected to him between June 2025 and April 2026, Houston Chronicle reported.
